info.name: Jenkins <=2.196 - Cookie Exposure
author: c-sh0
info.description: Jenkins through 2.196, LTS 2.176.3 and earlier prints the value of the cookie on the /whoAmI/ URL despite it being marked HttpOnly, thus making it possible to steal cookie-based authentication credentials if the URL is exposed or accessed via another cross-site scripting issue.
info.impact: The exposure of cookies can lead to session hijacking, unauthorized access, and potential data breaches.
info.remediation: Upgrade Jenkins to a version higher than 2.196 to mitigate the vulnerability.

info.name: Jenkins <=2.218 - Information Disclosure
author: c-sh0
info.description: Jenkins through 2.218, LTS 2.204.1 and earlier, is susceptible to information disclosure. An attacker can access exposed session identifiers on a user detail object in the whoAmI diagnostic page and thus potentially access sensitive information, modify data, and/or execute unauthorized operations.
info.impact: An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to gain sensitive information from the Jenkins server.
info.remediation: Upgrade Jenkins to a version higher than 2.218 to mitigate the vulnerability.

info.name: Apache Tomcat - HTTP Request Smuggling
author: 0x_akoko
info.description: Apache Tomcat from versions 8.5.0 to 8.5.93, 9.0.0-M1 to 9.0.81, lab-host-x-M1 to lab-host-x, and 11.0.0-M1 to 11.0.0-M11 contain an improper input validation caused by incorrect parsing of HTTP trailer headers, letting attackers craft headers to cause request smuggling, exploit requires sending malicious trailer headers.
info.impact: Attackers can perform request smuggling, potentially leading to cache poisoning, session hijacking, or bypassing security controls.
info.remediation: Upgrade to version 11.0.0-M12, lab-host-x, 9.0.81, or 8.5.94 or later.
